title: Nicola Cutcher
gist: A Prospect contributor index page for investigative journalist and documentary filmmaker Nicola Cutcher, listing five pieces concentrated on food-system capture (“Big Chicken is running our food strategy”), juror conscience, protest injunctions and childcare policy.

insights.claim: An investigative strand alleges that the UK's national food strategy is being run by the intensive poultry industry, published under the headline “Big Chicken is running our food strategy. Why?”
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Regulatory capture in agriculture is a policy risk for food producers and a reform target; worth tracking alongside UK food policy consultations.
insights.quote: Big Chicken is running our food strategy. Why?

insights.claim: The same investigative beat covers whether it is criminal for jurors to act on conscience and whether protest injunctions are out of order, framing the legal mechanics of climate protest rather than the protests themselves.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Civil injunctions and jury-direction rules, not headline sentences, are the real legal battleground for climate protest risk.
insights.locator: Is it criminal for jurors to act on conscience?

insights.claim: Childcare coverage is framed around the claim that the debate has forgotten the child, positioning outcomes for children against the prevailing economic-participation framing of childcare policy.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: A counter-frame to the labour-supply case for childcare subsidy that could surface in UK policy debate.
insights.quote: Have we forgotten the child in the childcare debate?
